title: (No AI) Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
author: Emma Roth
content:
![A collage of images generated by Canva Craft](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/04-CRAFT-COLLAGE.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, [called Canva Craft](https://www.canva.com/dream-lab), uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for "greater precision, consistency and control," according to [an announcement on Thursday](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-craft/).

title: (No AI) Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
author: Emma Roth
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/STK043_VRG_Illo_N_Barclay_1_Meta.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like _The Verge_ - but legal experts say these changes aren't enough to address their concerns. "This does nothing to restrict the 'associated with your products or services' \[language\] that would let Meta scrape entire sites," James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell Law School, [tells Nieman Lab](https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/10/legal-experts-warn-metas-new-terms-still-grant-broad-scraping-permissions-despite-language-changes/).
